source_text: τῷ δὲ βασιλεῖ τῶν αἰώνων, ἀφθάρτῳ, ἀοράτῳ, ⸀μόνῳ θεῷ, τιμὴ καὶ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
english_snapshot: To the King of the ages[a], immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read: "the only wise God."

source_text: καὶ ὁμολογουμένως μέγα ἐστὶν τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας μυστήριον· ⸀Ὃς ἐφανερώθη ἐν σαρκί, ἐδικαιώθη ἐν πνεύματι, ὤφθη ἀγγέλοις, ἐκηρύχθη ἐν ἔθνεσιν, ἐπιστεύθη ἐν κόσμῳ, ἀνελήμφθη ἐν δόξῃ.
english_snapshot:
And undeniably[a], great is the mystery of godliness:
He was revealed in flesh,
was vindicated in spirit,
was seen by angels,
was proclaimed among the nations,
was believed on in the world[d][c][b],
was taken up in glory.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'God was revealed in flesh' instead of 'He was revealed in flesh.' The critical Greek text reads 'who/he,' which is reflected here.

source_text: εἴ ⸀τις πιστὴ ἔχει χήρας, ⸀ἐπαρκείτω αὐταῖς, καὶ μὴ βαρείσθω ἡ ἐκκλησία, ἵνα ταῖς ὄντως χήραις ἐπαρκέσῃ.
english_snapshot: If any believing woman has widows[a], let her provide for them, and let the church not be burdened, so that it may provide for those who are truly widows.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'if any believing man or woman has widows' or 'if any believer has widows,' broadening the instruction beyond a specifically female subject.

source_text: ἥν τινες ἐπαγγελλόμενοι περὶ τὴν πίστιν ἠστόχησαν. Ἡ χάρις ⸂μεθ’ ὑμῶν⸃.
english_snapshot: By professing it[a], some have missed the mark concerning the faith[c][b]. Grace be with you.

signals.text: The Greek says 'with you' in the plural.
